text:
Jamie (support): Hey team, Customer ACME is seeing p95/p99 spikes on generate API since 02:00 UTC. They opened ticket #3421 with graphs — p99 went from ~600ms to 4.2s. Can someone take a look?
Mike (runtime): I can. Do we know which model/route and if there was a deploy around that time?
Jamie (support): Route: /v1/complete (redwood-hosted), model: rdx-large-v2, region us-west-2. Ticket has a heatmap showing lots of spikes aligned with a deploy at ~01:58.
deploy-bot: deployed rdx/rdx-middleware@release-2026-03-17 01:57:49 UTC to us-west-2 (canary -> prod) :rocket:
Anna (infra): Looking at infra metrics — KV cache eviction rate jumped 30x right after that deploy on several inference nodes. Miss rate went from 6% -> 48% on prefix-cache shard 12.
Mike (runtime): That smells like a cache key explosion. Any new headers or metadata keys added by middleware?
Sarah (ml): We shipped a middleware change that adds an "X-Session-Id" header for telemetry (release PR #789). If that header is not normalized it could create high cardinality keys used in prefix caching.
Kelsey (oncall): Can we confirm whether prefix cache keys include that header value? If so, that's the root cause. Quick mitigation: revert middleware or disable prefix-based caching for that route.
Mike (runtime): Quick grep on the serving logs shows prefixes like: 
```
prefix_key="model=rdx-large-v2|route=/v1/complete|x-session-id=9f2a.."
prefix_key="model=rdx-large-v2|route=/v1/complete|x-session-id=1b7c.."
```
So yes, the session id is being incorporated. That explains entropy.
Anna (infra): Repro on a canary node: run 1000 requests with unique X-Session-Id values -> eviction rate spikes and KV store evicts hot entries immediately. Repro script: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -H "X-Session-Id: sess-$i" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood/test/complete
done
```
Results attached to ticket.
Jamie (support): ACME confirmed they saw many clients with per-request session IDs (they already send session ids for their own infra tracing).
Kelsey (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback middleware release (short term), 2) enable cache key canonicalization to drop X-Session-Id for prefix cache, 3) enable temporary circuit-breaker to route to standby model if node p99 > 1s for >1m. Which can we do fastest?
Mike (runtime): I can roll back the middleware in us-west-2 now — reverting PR #789 from release-2026-03-17. Pushing rollback patch in 2m. Also I'll patch prefix cache to ignore headers named /^x-session-/ by config for all customer-facing routes; that needs a small runtime patch and will be rolled out canary first.
Anna (infra): Revert started by deploy-bot. Rollback in progress :arrow_down:
deploy-bot: rollback rdx-middleware -> release-2026-03-16 (triggered by Mike) in us-west-2 :white_check_mark:
Mike (runtime): Rollback completed. Monitoring p95/p99 now.
Sarah (ml): For a longer-term fix we should: - add a canonicalization step to prefix key generator that whitelists stable routing fields and drops high-cardinality headers - add unit tests that simulate header cardinality - add an opt-in config for customers who want to include session ids in metrics but not in cache keys.
Kelsey (oncall): Post-rollback: p99 for ACME dropped from 4.2s -> 580ms over the next 6 minutes. Still slightly elevated but heading down. Kelsey will keep the circuit-breaker rule active for another 20m.
Mike (runtime): Patch for key canonicalization (pseudocode): 
```
// canonicalize headers for cache key
allowed = ["host", "user-agent", "x-client-version"]
for (k,v) in request.headers:
  if k in allowed:
    kb.append(k+"="+normalize(v))
  // drop anything matching /^x-session-/
```
I'll open PR with tests.
Jamie (support): ACME confirms latency improved and thanked us. They asked whether this is something they triggered by using session ids per request. We'll draft a note explaining cache behavior and recommended headers.
Anna (infra): Additional cleanup: increase prefix-cache TTL from 30s -> 60s for the next 2 hours to help warmup while we patch key logic. Staggered warmup will be applied to avoid thundering herd.
Mike (runtime): Action items: 1) PR for canonicalization + tests (Mike) 2) Backport hotfix to prod after canary (Mike/Anna) 3) Postmortem + customer note (Jamie/Kelsey) 4) Add e2e test that runs high-cardinality header scenario (Sarah). I'll tag the PR with "hotfix/kv-key-canonicalize".
Kelsey (oncall): Thanks everyone. If p99 returns >1s after the next rollout we will escalate to incident channel. Closing here for now — keeping circuit-breaker in place until patch lands. :thumbsup:
